title: Resource Downloads & Next Steps
objectives: Download the U.S. Market Entry Checklist, Florida Setup Roadmap, Central Florida Resource Guide, and Expansion Decision Worksheet

contentBlocks.title: Your Takeaway Resources
contentBlocks.content:
With your readiness assessment complete, download the four resources that turn what you learned into an actionable plan:

  1. U.S. Market Entry Checklist. Module-by-module action list from legal setup to ecosystem resources.
  2. Florida Setup Roadmap. Step-by-step sequence from entity formation to fully operational.
  3. Central Florida Resource Guide. Directory of organizations, contacts, and programs for international founders.
  4. Expansion Decision Worksheet. Structured go/no-go framework to consider whether now is the right time.

Download all four now. They pair directly with your 1:1 meeting with [UCF BIP](https://incubator.ucf.edu).

contentBlocks.title: Did You Know?
contentBlocks.content: The UCF Business Incubation Program operates multiple sites across the greater Orlando region, providing over 100,000 square feet of incubation space. Since its founding, companies in the program have created thousands of jobs in Central Florida. UCF itself is one of the top patent-producing universities in the country, and the research partnerships between campus labs and incubator companies give founders access to talent and technology that would cost a fortune to build independently.

contentBlocks.title: Resource 1: U.S. Market Entry Checklist
contentBlocks.content:
This is your comprehensive checklist, every item, verified. The U.S. Market Entry Checklist turns every major topic from this program into action items grouped by module: legal setup, finances, IP protection, team building, market entry, culture, and ecosystem resources. Each item includes a priority level and suggested timeframe.

Tip: Start with the ecosystem section. It connects you with free resources before you start paying for services.

contentBlocks.title: Resource 2: Florida Setup Roadmap
contentBlocks.content:
This is your step-by-step sequence, what comes first, second, third. The Florida Setup Roadmap is sorted by order instead of topic, answering exactly that question. It walks through four phases: (1) pre-arrival preparation (remote), (2) entity formation and registration, (3) financial infrastructure, and (4) operational readiness. Each phase includes estimated timeframes and flags which steps require physical presence versus remote completion.

Many founders complete phases 1 and 2 remotely before arriving, so they can open a bank account in one visit with all documents ready.

contentBlocks.title: Resource 3: Central Florida Resource Guide
contentBlocks.content:
This guide puts every support organization one call away. The Central Florida Resource Guide puts all the groups from Module 7 into a single, easy-to-search reference. It covers business advising (SBDC, SCORE, [UCF BIP](https://incubator.ucf.edu)), incubators and accelerators, government programs (SBA, Enterprise Florida), professional services (attorneys, CPAs, banking contacts), networking and community organizations, and details on what comes after this course through [UCF BIP](https://incubator.ucf.edu).

Each entry includes the organization name, what they offer, and their website. Bookmark it and update it as you discover new resources through networking.

contentBlocks.title: Resource 4: Expansion Decision Worksheet
contentBlocks.content:
This is your go/no-go decision, the honest assessment before you commit. The Expansion Decision Worksheet helps you decide whether to enter the U.S. market now. It scores you across five areas: market fit, financial readiness, legal readiness, operations, and timing.

This is not pass/fail. A business owner from Colombia scored 2 out of 5 on financial readiness, spent four months strengthening home-market revenue, re-scored at 4, and entered the U.S. with a much stronger foundation. The worksheet tells you what gap to close first.

Complete this before your 1:1 meeting with [UCF BIP](https://incubator.ucf.edu). It helps the team give you targeted advice based on your specific readiness profile.

contentBlocks.title: Looking for the Full Resource Library?
contentBlocks.content: The full directory of organizations, tools, and links lives on the dedicated Resources page (also accessible from your dashboard). It includes everything covered in this lesson plus categorized links for legal formation, tax/banking, IP, visas, free support orgs, and UCF BIP next steps. Bookmark it; we keep it updated.

contentBlocks.title: Entrepreneur organizing resources and preparation materials for U.S. market entry
Match Your Situation to the Right Takeaway Resource
contentBlocks.description: You have four downloadable resources. Each serves a different purpose. Pick which fits each founder's situation, then check the explanation.

paths.label: Sara just finalized her business plan and wants a single document that lists every action item across all 8 modules, organized by topic
paths.outcome: U.S. Market Entry Checklist. The checklist organizes every major topic from the program (legal, taxes, IP, hiring, customers, culture, ecosystem) into action items with priority levels and timeframes. Sara can use it as her master to-do list and check items off as she completes them. Best for founders who think topic-by-topic.

paths.label: Carlos wants to know exactly what to do first, second, and third, in chronological order, from "I am still in my home country" to "I am operational in Florida"
paths.outcome: Florida Setup Roadmap. The roadmap is sorted by sequence (not by topic). It walks through four phases: pre-arrival preparation (you can do this remotely), entity formation and registration, financial infrastructure, and operational readiness. Best for founders who want to know "what comes next" rather than "what topics exist." It also flags which steps require physical presence in Florida vs. which you can complete from home.

paths.label: Aisha needs to find local mentors, attorneys, banks, and support organizations, with names and contact info she can actually call
paths.outcome: Central Florida Resource Guide. The guide is the single-document directory of every support organization, professional service, and program covered in Module 7. It includes business advising (SBDC, SCORE, UCF BIP), incubators, government programs, attorneys, CPAs, banking contacts, and networking organizations. Best when you have already decided to act and now need names and numbers.

paths.label: Hiroshi is 90% sure he wants to expand to the U.S., but his board wants a structured go/no-go before approving the budget
paths.outcome: Expansion Decision Worksheet. The worksheet scores readiness across five dimensions: market fit, financial readiness, legal readiness, operations, and timing. It is a decision tool, not a pass/fail test. A founder from Colombia scored 2 out of 5 on financial readiness, spent four months strengthening home-market revenue, re-scored at 4, and entered the U.S. with a much stronger foundation. Hiroshi can complete it before his board meeting and use the output to drive the conversation.

questions.stem: A founder has validated her market opportunity and wants to know the correct ORDER of steps to become operational in Florida, from entity formation through financial setup to hiring. Which downloadable resource is specifically designed for this purpose?
options: U.S. Market Entry Checklist, it covers every topic from the program in checklist format
Florida Setup Roadmap, it organizes steps by sequence (what to do first, second, third) rather than by topic
Expansion Decision Worksheet, it helps assess whether to enter the U.S. market at all
Central Florida Resource Guide, it lists organizations and contacts available to founders
questions.explanation: The Florida Setup Roadmap is organized by sequence rather than by topic. It walks entrepreneurs through four phases: pre-arrival preparation, entity formation, financial infrastructure, and operational readiness, in the correct order. The Checklist organizes by module topic, while the Roadmap answers 'what do I do first, second, third?'

questions.stem: A founder completed the Expansion Decision Worksheet and scored high on market fit but low on financial readiness. Based on the lesson guidance, what is the most strategic response?
options: Enter the U.S. market immediately since market fit is the most important factor
Abandon U.S. expansion plans entirely since financial readiness is insufficient
Strengthen home-market revenue first to improve financial readiness, then revisit the worksheet before entering the U.S.
Apply for an SBA loan to cover the financial gap before entering the market
questions.explanation: The Expansion Decision Worksheet is not a pass/fail test. A founder from Colombia used it, found her financial score was 2 out of 5, spent four months strengthening home-market revenue, and re-scored at 4 before entering the U.S. with a stronger foundation. The worksheet tells you what gap to close first, not whether to give up.

questions.stem: A founder has completed this program and is preparing to meet with the UCF BIP team. What is the best way to make the most of the 1:1 meeting?
options: Arrive with the Expansion Decision Worksheet completed and specific questions ready, so the team can give targeted advice based on her readiness profile
Arrive unprepared and let the team decide what to discuss
Focus the meeting on pitching her product rather than discussing market readiness
Ask the team to make business decisions on her behalf during the meeting
questions.explanation: The 1:1 meeting with the UCF BIP team works best when you arrive with the Expansion Decision Worksheet completed and specific questions ready. That lets the team give focused advice based on your specific readiness profile rather than starting from scratch. The meeting is to guide you, not to pitch your product or have the team make decisions for you.

contentBlocks.title: Key Takeaway
contentBlocks.content: Download these resources before your 1:1 meeting with UCF BIP. They extend the value of this program from the screen into your actual planning. The checklist keeps you organized. The roadmap keeps you in sequence. The resource guide connects you to help. The decision worksheet keeps you honest about readiness. Download all four now and bring them to your 1:1 meeting with the [UCF BIP](https://incubator.ucf.edu) team.
